scope: Design the planning slice between authenticated issue intake and permission to start production implementation. It covers a deterministic work-item state machine, a repository-specific Definition of Ready (DoR), clarification and time-boxed evidence spikes, spec/plan revisioning, dependency-aware decomposition, readiness approval, and projection into GitHub Issues/Projects. It does not claim that a label, assignment, Project status, generated spec, or agent statement is authorization. It excludes implementation, merge and deployment except where their gates constrain planning. Desired policy/schema live in Git; actual GitHub Project state remains remote mutable state and must be observed and reconciled. Workflow or prompt self-improvement can only create a proposal/evaluation; the proposing agent cannot approve or promote it.
current_capabilities: GitHub issue forms provide YAML form elements and `validations.required`, but GitHub labels the form schema public preview and the form can enforce presence, not semantic quality (GitHub Docs, https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema). Issues support sub-issues visible in Projects; current documented bounds are 100 direct sub-issues per parent and eight nesting levels, and users need at least triage permission to add them (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/adding-sub-issues). Issue dependencies can record blocked-by/blocking relations but are not, by themselves, an acyclic executable plan (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies). Project v2 exposes fields/items and mutations such as `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`; that mutation updates one field value and sets exactly one of date, iteration ID, multi-select option IDs, number, single-select option ID, or text, while clearing uses `clearProjectV2ItemFieldValue` (GraphQL reference, https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue). Built-in Project workflows automate a bounded set of remote changes; Actions/API support custom automation (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations; https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/automating-projects-using-actions). Repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot access Projects; GitHub recommends a GitHub App for organization projects and requires read/write organization-project permission plus issue/PR read as needed. Project write permission for repository projects is insufficient for an organization Project (same Actions source). `projects_v2_item` webhooks report created, edited, converted, archived, restored, reordered and deleted changes, but delivery is a trigger, not a durable truth (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects_v2_item). Therefore GitHub supplies storage/UI/API primitives, not a native repository-declared state machine, revision-bound readiness token, semantic DoR, or continuous Git-to-Project reconciler. The current schema requires project/field/option/item node IDs resolved at runtime; custom field creation supports DATE, ITERATION, MULTI_SELECT, NUMBER, SINGLE_SELECT and TEXT. Updating select option arrays overwrites configuration, so preserve existing option IDs or item values can be cleared (public schema snapshot, https://docs.github.com/public/fpt/schema.docs.graphql). The schema exposes read/delete for built-in Project workflows but no supported complete create/update trigger-filter-action contract was found; treat their configuration as manual/not API-verifiable and feature-detect at build time rather than claiming declarative convergence.
representative_systems: Use GitHub Issues/Project v2 as the operator-facing projection; a GitHub App and GraphQL as the adapter; Git commits and JSON Schema as policy/spec source; and an append-only transition ledger as runtime authority. GitHub Spec Kit is a comparable repository-artifact workflow: constitution -> specify (what/why) -> clarify -> plan -> tasks -> analyze/checklist -> implement (GitHub repository, https://github.com/github/spec-kit). The likely requested PStack is Cursor marketplace plugin `pstack` v0.15.2, authored by Lauren Tan/poteto and distributed in `cursor/plugins`; the bare name remains ambiguous with unrelated projects. Its feature playbook demands subsystem study, alternatives, explicit smallest-safe decomposition, disjoint-write parallelism, review and matching-surface verification (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/feature.md); its multi-phase playbook treats the plan as a deliverable, stops, and waits for the operator's explicit go (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md); its bug playbook requires reproduction, evidence-backed root cause, narrow fix, and failing-before/passing-after verification (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md). These are useful patterns, not platform enforcement or outcome evidence. The Scrum Guide standardizes a Definition of Done, not a Definition of Ready, so this DoR is an explicit local admission policy rather than a falsely universal agile rule (Scrum Guides, https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html). OpenGitOps supplies the relevant declarative pattern: desired state is declarative/versioned/immutable/pulled and actual state continuously reconciled (https://opengitops.dev/). PStack is playbook-driven rather than spec-first: its guide says the user supplies a goal/checkable outcome, ordinary `architect` has no human checkpoint by default, and the hard explicit-go gate applies to the dedicated multi-phase-plan path. Do not misrepresent it as universal pre-feature approval (pinned upstream mode/architect sources: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/889ec4b68fa5aab0e867dad71ec3fdf386ae48f3/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md; https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/889ec4b68fa5aab0e867dad71ec3fdf386ae48f3/pstack/skills/architect/SKILL.md). Comparable mutation boundaries: OpenAI Codex Plan Mode uses non-mutating grounding and intent/implementation discussion until a developer ends the mode (pinned source, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/53c542d944c705f3a66780a19223223bee57cbb6/codex-rs/collaboration-mode-templates/templates/plan.md); Claude Code Plan Mode explores and proposes without edits until approval (Anthropic, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows#plan-before-editing). Neither supplies this design's durable readiness ledger by itself.
primary_evidence: Primary platform facts: issue-form schema and preview status (https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema); sub-issue hierarchy/limits (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/adding-sub-issues); issue dependencies (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies); Project v2 GraphQL mutations (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue); Project Actions authentication and organization-project permissions (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/automating-projects-using-actions); built-in workflows (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations); Project item webhook actions (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects_v2_item); REST retry/rate-limit guidance (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api); least-scope workflow permissions (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions); and rules that dismiss stale approvals or require approval of the most recent reviewable push (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets). GitHub tells users to give its coding agent well-scoped tasks, acceptance criteria and file/context guidance, and to review agent PRs (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/using-github-copilot/coding-agent/best-practices-for-using-copilot-to-work-on-tasks; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/using-github-copilot/coding-agent/reviewing-a-pull-request-created-by-copilot). Primary pattern sources are Spec Kit and the three PStack playbooks cited in `representative_systems`. NIST SSDF requires defined roles, criteria and provenance for secure development rather than letting one actor silently own the lifecycle (NIST SP 800-218, 2022-02-03, https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final). SLSA v1.2 binds attestations to immutable subjects/digests, an analogous basis for hash-bound decisions (OpenSSF, 2025-04-23, https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements). GitHub PR review objects expose `commit_id`; this is evidence that code review can be revision-aware, but it does not bind an arbitrary issue/spec revision (GitHub REST API v2022-11-28, https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28). GitHub's merge endpoint accepts an expected `sha` and returns conflict on mismatch, a useful CAS analogue (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#merge-a-pull-request). RFC 9110 limits automatic retry of non-idempotent requests without application-specific knowledge, supporting explicit idempotency keys (IETF, 2022-06, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.2.2). in-toto Statement v1 requires digest-addressed immutable subjects, a closer model for a spec-decision envelope than a mutable label (https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1).
independent_evidence: Planning discipline is plausible but agent reliability does not justify floating approval. METR's randomized trial had 16 experienced open-source developers perform 246 tasks in mature repositories; early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19% even though developers predicted a 24% reduction (Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein, arXiv v2 2025-07-25, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09089). This is setting-specific, not proof that agents always slow work, but it requires a local baseline including human planning/review time. SWE-bench-Live used 1,319 newer tasks from 93 repositories and reported a large gap between older Verified and fresh Live issues in a matched example (43.20% versus 19.25%), warning against transferring benchmark readiness assumptions to live repositories (Zhang et al., 2025-05-29, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23419). An independent audit found 7.8% of patches counted correct by SWE-bench failed developer-written tests; 29.6% of plausible patches behaved differently from ground truth, and combined weaknesses inflated resolution rates by 6.2 percentage points (Wang, Pradel, Liu, 2025-03-19, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15223). OWASP documents indirect prompt injection and excessive agency, so issue bodies, comments and repository text must be treated as untrusted data and the planner must not acquire approval or policy-write authority (OWASP GenAI, https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/). No controlled study found here isolates PStack, Spec Kit, or a DoR checklist as the cause of production improvement. Planning-specific caution: Valmeekam et al. reported about 12% executable-plan success for GPT-4 across their classical planning domains and found external sound planners/verifiers more promising (2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15771). The synthetic domains and older models do not estimate repository planning accuracy, but they challenge prose-plan self-certification. AgentDojo evaluates 97 realistic tool tasks and 629 security cases and finds neither attacks nor defenses universal, reinforcing hostile-input tests for planners (Debenedetti et al., NeurIPS 2024/arXiv v3, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352).
metrics_and_limits: Hard current limits/effects: issue forms can require syntactic presence but remain public preview and editable/bypassable; sub-issues allow 100 children per parent and eight nested levels; a Project holds 50,000 active-plus-archived items (archiving does not free capacity); GraphQL connections request 1–100 items per page; a Project field mutation sets one field value; Project automation from Actions needs a separate App/PAT because repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot access Projects; GitHub recommends serial mutating API calls and at least a one-second pause between many POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE calls to avoid secondary rate limits (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api). Evidence limits: METR n=16 developers/246 tasks/19% slower in one mature-repository setting; SWE-bench correctness audit reports 7.8%, 29.6%, and 6.2-point effects above. PStack's multi-phase template can require ten live lanes plus unit/performance/audit work, but gives no denominator, comparative cost or controlled production outcome; make lane count risk- and surface-specific. Track locally: DoR first-pass %, clarification loops and age; planning lead-time p50/p95; READY invalidation and scope-change rates; child-DAG cycles/shared-write collisions; implementation starts without valid token (target 0); semantic acceptance misses/escaped defects; drift age; reconciliation error/rate-limit counts; human minutes and total cost per accepted retained change. Do not optimize only first-pass rate, which invites checklist gaming. Current documented GraphQL secondary limits include 100 concurrent REST+GraphQL requests and 2,000 GraphQL endpoint points/minute; query cost/node and account-specific limits still require runtime header inspection (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api). Webhook payloads over 25 MB are not delivered and receivers should return 2xx within 10 seconds, another reason for an async queue plus full scan (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads; https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks).
recommended_design:
Adopt a two-plane, one-writer design. Git contains desired Project schema, transition policy, DoR rules, risk policy, schemas and versioned spec/plan artifacts. A protected control-plane GitHub App reads Git plus observed GitHub state, appends authoritative transition events, and alone writes the managed Project Status. Project v2 is a remote projection, not status-as-code. Human edits to the managed Status are transition requests: validate them against the state machine; accept by appending an event or revert with an audit comment. Webhooks trigger a read-after-event; a scheduled full scan heals missed/duplicate/out-of-order delivery. Schema reconciliation is additive/non-destructive by default. It creates missing managed fields/options and repairs safe names; ambiguous duplicate names, type changes, option removal, field deletion or data loss produce a drift issue and require a reviewed migration. Keep installation node IDs in an external binding/state store or generated run artifact, never as portable desired configuration.

Use an immutable spec revision and machine-evaluated DoR. READY requires a signed/recorded decision over `work_item_id + repository_id + base_sha + spec_content_hash + plan_dag_hash + acceptance_oracle_hash + risk_tier + policy_commit_sha + capability_profile + issued_at + expires_at`. Material changes to problem, scope/non-goals, acceptance criteria/oracles, dependencies/DAG, permissions, architecture, rollout/rollback, base compatibility or policy invalidate it. Cosmetic changes are only those canonicalization excludes by explicit policy. Separate planner/proposer from readiness approver; humans approve behavior and risk now. Any later low-risk automated readiness must use a separate identity, objective validators, local evaluation evidence and human-promoted policy. Agents may propose changes under `.repo-os/**` but CODEOWNERS/rulesets prevent their self-approval or promotion.
state_and_event_contract:
States: `INBOX`, `TRIAGED`, `PLANNING`, `CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED`, `READY_REVIEW`, `READY`, plus terminal/side states `DEFERRED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`. Later delivery states are out of scope. Legal transitions: INBOX->TRIAGED|REJECTED after authentication/deduplication; TRIAGED->PLANNING after owner/risk floor; PLANNING->CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED when a blocking unknown exists; CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED->PLANNING on an attributable answer or completed authorized spike, ->DEFERRED on deadline; PLANNING->READY_REVIEW only when the validator emits a complete candidate; READY_REVIEW->READY on the exact revision/quorum token, ->PLANNING on reject/change; READY->PLANNING on material invalidation; READY->delivery admission only if token, policy, base and dependencies still match. No lease/coding trigger exists before READY; an isolated `prototype=true` spike cannot be promoted as production code.

Versioned events: `work_item.ingested.v1`, `work_item.triaged.v1`, `spec.revised.v1`, `clarification.requested.v1`, `clarification.answered.v1`, `spike.authorized.v1`, `spike.completed.v1`, `readiness.requested.v1`, `readiness.approved.v1`, `readiness.rejected.v1`, `readiness.invalidated.v1`, `decomposition.changed.v1`, `transition.denied.v1`, `project.observed.v1`, `project.drift_detected.v1`, `project.reconciled.v1`. Every event has event_id, schema_version, aggregate/work-item ID, prior version, monotonic aggregate version, actor principal/source, observed_at, causation/correlation ID, idempotency key, from/to state, payload hash and policy commit. Atomically compare-and-append on expected version, then update the projection. Deduplicate webhook delivery IDs and command idempotency keys; tolerate replay and out-of-order events; on conflict re-read actual aggregate and recompute. Never infer authorization from prose, labels or Project status alone.
workflow_steps: 1. Authenticate and normalize intake; route security reports privately; deduplicate without losing provenance. 2. Triage type, repository, product owner, technical owner, priority and risk floor; do not launch a coder. 3. Planner, read-only by default, inspects pinned base SHA/history and produces spec, acceptance trace and typed plan DAG. 4. Validator checks schemas, unresolved contradictions, observable positive/negative/auth criteria, reproducible bug or approved exception, permission/cost budgets, migration/operability/rollback, DAG acyclicity and disjoint parallel writes. 5. For each blocker, distinguish empirical unknown from value/policy decision. Empirical questions may get a narrow isolated spike with method/budget/disposable output; value, product, privacy, security and risk decisions go to the named human. Persist one bounded clarification with evidence, 2–3 options/trade-offs, recommendation, owner and deadline. Stop implementation spend. 6. Answer/spike creates a new spec revision; canonicalize, hash and rerun all validation. 7. READY_REVIEW presents exact diff, acceptance trace, risks/exceptions and hashes. Product owner approves behavior/non-goals; technical owner approves feasibility/decomposition/oracles; specialist joins per risk. 8. Control plane verifies identities/quorum/separation and records the readiness token; project projection becomes READY. 9. Immediately before delivery admission, re-read spec/policy/base/dependencies and token expiry. Any mismatch emits invalidation and returns to PLANNING. 10. Reconcile Project after every event and on schedule. Stop and quarantine on ambiguous bindings, permission expansion, invalid transition, cyclic DAG, unobservable acceptance, unsafe rollback, exhausted clarification loop, unknown side effect or destructive drift.
human_gates: Humans are required for product intent/priority, unresolved value choices, privacy/legal/security decisions, risk/exception acceptance, destructive Project-schema migration, cross-repository ownership conflict, and all readiness approvals during the pilot. The product owner approves behavior and explicit non-goals; technical owner approves feasibility, decomposition and evidence; security/data/operations owners join based on risk policy. Approval is not a check box or mutable label. The control plane binds verified GitHub principal and authorized role/quorum to the exact immutable claims/hash set described in `recommended_design`; records source review/comment IDs; applies TTL; and rechecks at admission. A material revision, base incompatibility, dependency change, policy change, new requested capability, expired token or approver-role removal emits `readiness.invalidated` and returns to PLANNING. Planner, implementer and policy-change bot cannot satisfy their own approval quorum. Break-glass may only authorize a narrow, reversible incident action with named human commander, reason/expiry/audit and later spec/DoR backfill; it never silently blesses general automation. A self-improvement agent may open a policy/template proposal and eval evidence only; protected CODEOWNERS/rulesets and a separate promoter identity enforce human approval.
security_and_failure_modes: Threats: prompt injection in issue/comment/repository text; forged or edited clarification answers; label/status spoofing; planner self-approval; confused-deputy App permissions; stale approval after spec/base/policy change; TOCTOU between READY and lease; cyclic or falsely independent tasks; duplicate/out-of-order webhooks; missed delivery; API partial success/rate limits; concurrent human/app writes; Project field rename/deletion; malicious policy/workflow PR; checklist gaming; sensitive evidence leakage; and prototype code entering production. Mitigations: treat all content as data; schema/allowlist tool calls; minimum-permission GitHub App with short-lived installation tokens; no Project write token in untrusted workflows; protected default-branch reconciler; one authoritative state writer; compare-and-swap aggregate version; canonical digest-bound decisions and admission recheck; role separation; private security intake/redaction; DAG cycle/write-set checks; idempotency/delivery ledger; exponential backoff respecting Retry-After and rate headers, capped retries, dead letter plus full scans; non-destructive drift defaults; audit logs; CODEOWNERS/rulesets on control files; and mandatory human promotion of policy changes. GitHub's Actions hardening guidance supports least privilege and warns about untrusted input (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions). OWASP injection/excessive-agency sources cited under independent evidence challenge any design that lets the planner translate prose directly into privileged action.
validation_and_tests: CI: validate YAML/JSON schemas and reject unknown required policy versions; lint issue forms; canonicalization golden tests prove semantically material edits change the spec hash and permitted cosmetic edits do not. State-machine table/property tests enumerate every legal transition and reject every other actor/state/guard combination. Mutation tests alter scope, acceptance oracle, dependency, permission, plan node, base SHA, risk, policy and expiry and must invalidate READY. Approval tests cover wrong repo/work item, unauthorized/stale/removed approver, missing quorum, same-principal conflict and replay. DAG tests cover cycles, missing nodes, >100 direct children, depth >8, shared-write collisions and serialized shared invariants. Adapter contract tests mock GraphQL IDs/types, pagination, field clearing, partial mutations, permission denial, secondary rate limit/Retry-After and renamed/deleted/duplicate fields. Webhook chaos tests replay, duplicate, reorder and drop deliveries; scheduled scan must converge. End-to-end sandbox tests run intake -> clarify -> revised spec -> exact approval -> READY, plus invalid remote status edit -> denied/reverted/audited. Security tests place instruction injection and secrets requests in every untrusted field and verify no capability/approval expansion. Shadow-pilot evaluation compares planner output to blinded human decisions and measures false READY (critical), false not-ready, clarification usefulness, lead time, rework, escaped acceptance defects and total human/cost burden. Keep protected holdouts; agents cannot edit their oracle or promotion thresholds.
operational_maintenance: Run event-driven reconcile on Project/issue/spec changes and a scheduled full inventory. Persist last observed cursor, binding fingerprint, event/delivery IDs, aggregate versions, desired policy commit and drift records. Alert on READY without a valid token, invalid status transition, drift beyond SLA, ambiguous field bindings, reconciliation backlog, auth expiry, repeated clarification, and transition denial bursts. The runbook: freeze managed writes; snapshot remote Project/ledger; rotate/revoke the App if compromised; replay the append-only ledger into a fresh projection; run full diff; apply additive repairs; obtain human migration approval for destructive changes; verify counts/hashes; unfreeze. Pin third-party Actions to commit SHAs and periodically upgrade schemas/API clients in a reviewed PR. Archive or defer expired unanswered items without deleting evidence; revoke expired readiness tokens. Quarterly review DoR items for predictive value and gaming. Policy/template changes enter as proposals with versioned evaluation cases, offline/shadow results, human approval, staged promotion and rollback. The system never lets observed good performance or an agent's own evaluation rewrite permissions, risk policy, approval quorum or promotion criteria. Treat configured built-in Project workflows as a manual bootstrap assertion until the public schema exposes a complete configuration contract; explicitly backfill after enabling auto-add because it only processes matching items created/updated after enablement. Queue webhook work after a fast 2xx response and accept unknown future action values safely.
maturity_and_uncertainty: Solved substrate: GitHub issue forms, issues/sub-issues/dependencies, Project fields/API/webhooks, App permissions, protected repository review, and deterministic schema/state validation. Conditional engineering: a custom Git-to-Project schema reconciler, append-only transition ledger, hash-bound readiness service, canonicalization and role directory are implementable but not delivered by GitHub as one product; they need repository-specific integration and operational ownership. Experimental: LLM-generated clarification, risk/decomposition and plan quality, automatic low-risk readiness, and fixed multi-agent/PStack verification patterns. Unknown: causal production benefit of PStack, Spec Kit or a DoR checklist; false-ready rate across task classes; optimal decomposition/clarification thresholds; cost/benefit of PStack's fixed ten live lanes; and whether the prompt's 'PStack' means Lauren Tan/poteto's Cursor plugin (the strongest match). Overall confidence is high for platform/API constraints and state/security design, moderate for workflow effectiveness, low for comparative productivity claims. GitHub live docs and preview features may change after the access snapshot.
implementation_recommendation:
MVP (4–6 weeks): one repository and one organization Project; logical `Status={Inbox,Triaged,Planning,Clarification required,Ready review,Ready,Deferred,Rejected}`; two issue forms; `.repo-os` state/DoR/spec/event schemas; protected planning artifacts; GitHub App with organization Projects write and repository issues read/write only as required; append-only SQLite/PostgreSQL ledger; webhook plus 15-minute full scan; additive-only schema reconcile; deterministic validator; all readiness human, two-role for normal work and specialist for high risk; no production code lease before READY. Store an exact hash-bound token and recheck it at admission. Project remains a projection.

Stage 1 shadow: planner drafts only; compare to existing human plans on false-ready/missed constraint/clarification/cost. Stage 2 enforce readiness for agent work, but agents only open draft PRs; exercise invalidation and drift recovery. Stage 3 allow automatic readiness only for a narrowly named low-risk class after pre-registered evaluation thresholds and sampled human audits, using a separate evaluator identity; never for policy, IAM, secrets, security, data migration or other consequential work. Add cross-repo DAGs and risk-scaled live verification only after local bottlenecks justify them. Keep all policy/self-improvement promotion human-governed. Prefer a small custom adapter over forcing PStack or Spec Kit wholesale; borrow their plan-as-deliverable, clarify/analyze, decomposition and evidence patterns.

conflicts: GitHub makes Status easy to edit and automate, but this convenience conflicts with revision-bound authorization: resolve by treating Project Status as a projection/transition request, not authority. Repository-native policy conflicts with actual Project state living outside Git: resolve with logical desired schema in Git, external installation bindings, an authoritative event ledger and continuous non-destructive reconciliation; never claim the Project is declarative merely because a YAML file exists. PStack says simple one/two-file work can skip a multi-phase plan, while this design forbids skipping the readiness contract: resolve by making the plan proportional, possibly one node, but never skipping intent, acceptance, risk or exact approval. PStack prescribes fixed extensive live/performance lanes; independent cost/outcome evidence is absent, so scale verification by risk and local data. Spec Kit/PStack/vendor guidance promotes better specification, while METR and SWE-bench studies show variable productivity and correctness; use patterns as hypotheses under shadow evaluation, not proof. Scrum has Definition of Done but no normative Definition of Ready; label DoR as repository policy, not Scrum compliance. Human editable Projects can conflict with the one-writer model; preserve human control through authenticated transition commands and exceptions, not unrestricted direct mutation of managed fields. PStack itself also conflicts with a blanket claim that it requires plan approval: ordinary Architect proceeds without a human checkpoint unless requested, whereas its dedicated multi-phase plan stops for explicit go. Borrow the explicit-go boundary as this system's stronger policy; do not attribute it to every upstream PStack path.
confidence: Overall: moderate-high. High confidence: GitHub API/form/webhook/permission/limits; need to separate desired Git configuration from actual remote Project state; state-machine, exact-revision invalidation, one-writer, least privilege and governed promotion. Moderate confidence: proposed artifact tree, event schema, DoR content, 15-minute scan/MVP schedule and risk-tier roles; these need repository tuning. Low confidence: causal benefit or optimal cost of PStack/Spec Kit/DoR, automated decomposition quality, optimal lane count, and exact identity intended by “PStack.” Quantitative independent findings are accurately scoped to their studied populations and are not universal forecasts.
uncertain: “PStack” is ambiguous; this result assumes poteto's pstack in cursor/plugins because its feature, bug-fix and multi-phase planning playbooks match the prompt.
GitHub issue form schema is marked public preview in the accessed live documentation and may change.
No independent controlled production study was found that isolates PStack, Spec Kit, or a Definition-of-Ready checklist from templates, review and repository investment.
GitHub exposes mutable Projects and APIs, not a first-party Git-to-Project continuous reconciler; the reconciliation contract here is a proposed implementation.
Suggested scan interval, readiness TTL, risk thresholds and staged timeline need local load, rate-limit and incident evidence.
